answers.T1: To-do: there are two things this month, the Taiwan crisis and a staff proposal; go through them in order and then press Execute. I would first press one of the three answer boxes under the crisis, probably Joint patrol with Japan since it says my Defense Secretary backs it. The orange box says 'Pick an answer above first' so I understand it waits for me.
answers.T2: Eight things, two done (the bar and 'Handled' count say so). The CNN interview: it says skipped, a deputy answers, so someone else goes in my place. If I press Execute now, six items not handled: deputies take three meetings and two proposals do not run. I had to read the small print at the bottom to know that.
answers.T3: Orange one: I take the call myself and say my answer. Middle one: I accept what the Secretary of State suggests and I still attend. Dashed one: I send a deputy with the default answer, it costs nothing, but Xi notices I was not there. To avoid bother I press the dashed one; a deputy goes and Xi is a bit offended. The word 'staff pick' is slightly odd to me but I follow it.
answers.T4: Court India will not run this month and my one point stays in the bank. Yes, there is an Undo button, two of them. Later I would look at the 'Skipped' heading on the right under the staff picks.
answers.T5: Three of eight handled, now the Takaichi visit. From the map I answer in the box on the left, or press Desk. The green button approves three staff picks that wait: Takaichi visit, Court India and Intel on China, for two points. The map itself is mostly blobs; I would rather be on the desk.
answers.T6: Can press: Execute month, Approve, Guided/Full desk, the three answer boxes, the underlined blue links, the cards on the left. Cannot press: the stat numbers at the top, the paragraph of crisis text, the picture. Not sure about: the 'Next: Takaichi visits' button (I think it presses), the top numbers like approval, the green ticks, and the 'Skipped' dashed boxes (they have Undo inside, but is the whole box pressable?).
answers.T7: B has the items as a row across the top, so the left side is gone and the main text is wider; I can see all eight at a glance. But the last tab is cut off at the edge and the labels are small. A has the list down the left with bigger text and the 'handled' bar, easier to read on a tablet. B makes it harder to see the status words and it might run off the screen. A makes me scroll down in the left column to find orders.

agenda.verbatim: I like A. It tells me in plain words what to do: go through these, in order, and press Execute at the end. The three boxes at the bottom are clear once I read them, though 'staff pick' and 'send a deputy' took me a moment. What I do not like is how much small writing there is, and the keys line is not for me. B squeezes the list across the top and I lose the text; I would rather have the list on the left. As for the little pictures I was shown, about half I could not tell without words, so please keep the words next to them.
